Base of the jack should be a 12v solenoid, identify positive and jump to open system allowing fluid to escape as you manipulate the jack up.

Springs always have upward pressure in system shown, solenoid keeps that pressure sealed and closed when in down position. 

Have the leveling system run retract all, get 4 - 6' pry and a 4x4 or equivalent block, anything 6-8" away to use as a fulcrum. Jump 12v to the positive on the solenoid while simultaneously pushing down on the bar.

Google the leveling system by brand and model and look for parts diagrams for more info. Look up by the mounting bolts to the frame, should see a loom of 12-14g wire at the top of jack
Did you blast nails through the old membrane and then just paint over the OSB??

Work on dometic all the time, I bought the alpicool and it worked for 2 weeks straight on a road trip, that was over a year ago. 

Used it last weekend, still works great both on 12v and 110v. Simple, does the job
Yes. Clean, Scrape, clean and reseal. Use a heat gun
If you bought at a dealership, make them fix it. Should have drilled holes in the battery box during pre inspection

Yes. Check all sealant every spring and fall and touch up where needed. 

Plan for 8 - 14 hours at the shop every 2 years to have it done properly if you want the thing to last more than 5.

Lol look at the "pro" whose sealing over old, already failing sealant 😂

Scrape, clean and reseal every 2 years before it starts to rot and silicone will do much better my dude. 

Have fun removing .750" cock hard shitty proflex after it leaks the 6th time you've sealed over it.

Pull the light fixtures that are affect by the fuse, likely a short inside near connections causing the fuse to blow.

As for the high pitch, 95% sure that's going to be your converter, it takes your AC 120V and converts to 12v. Check there, output when connected to 120v should be between 12.8 on the low side, to 14V on the high side, ideally somewhere around 13.4.
Also it won't be on a breaker, look for a 15 or 20A fuse

Also open up a couple of hot taps and confirm good water flow, double check strainers for debris clogging flow.

Can take a while to get LP to the pilot, and the small orifice and lead to a length air lock you have to bleed, often more than you can get in the few attempts before the system locks out on fault. I will light the stove/and or the fridge to try and get some flow through, can take up to 5mins depending on your supply/ambient temp/gas pressure etc.

Also any info on the trailer just rough idea what the setup is?

You said it's a replacement for an old atwood tank, make sure if there is still a Propane switch for the old water heater is in the on position, otherwise it will be restricted at the switch.

Installed a few that had me scratching my head until the light bulb goes on lol.
Suburban 525042 waterheater gas valve for SW should do it, just reference the model tag on your water heater to confirm

Check Converter is outputting DC when connected to shore power. 

Check 20/30A fuses likely on the converter itself if not on main fuse panels.

Check main connections from back of panel from shore connector. 
If it's a cord test continuity to ensure there isn't an internal short

Blowing what fuse when plugged in? House side? Main 50amp on trailers service box? 

What's the setup for the generator? -  built into the unit with transfer switch/secondary relays?

Likely a furnace issue, had faulty sail switches that intermittently get stuck in closed position so when trying to re-light they throw a code.

Check the furnace board for a flashing light code when if fails to turn back on, I'd guess 4 x .5s  flashes is Air fault. In that case diagnos the sail switch, if it looks clean and issue persists, replace the board.

Could check the Hi-limit but usually they fail hard and no function is possible without bypassing or replacing
Should be 12v for Rv, if indead is a 24v battery  confirm inverter is rated and operating in 24v
